values.name: Solid red
values.description: Constant-color Picture rendered to a 16×16 image. The simplest possible Field.

values.name: Centred circle
values.description: Red circle radius 5 at (8, 8), rendered at 16×16. The math: Field(\p -> if dist p c <= r then col else transparent).

values.name: Circle on blue
values.description: Composition: red circle layered over a solid blue background using `over`.

values.name: Sinusoidal stripes
values.description: Vertical bands: red where sin(0.5·x) > 0, blue otherwise. The math: \p -> if sin(0.5·p.x) > 0 then red else blue.

values.name: Diagonal gradient
values.description: Pure math: r = 8·x, g = 8·y, b = 4·(x+y). Color emerges from coordinates — no shape primitives.

values.name: Checkerboard
values.description: Classic interference pattern: floor(x/4) + floor(y/4) mod 2 picks alternating colors.

values.name: Radial sine rings
values.description: Concentric rings from sin(distance·1.2). The whole image emerges from one math expression — no nested shapes, just radial math.

values.name: Radial gradient
values.description: Color smoothly interpolated by distance: closer to center = brighter red. \p -> color(255 · max(0, 1 - d/16), 0, 0, 255).

values.name: Interference (sine grid)
values.description: Two sines crossed: sin(x·0.5) · sin(y·0.5). Where both peak the result is bright; where they cancel it goes dark.

values.name: Diagonal stripes (modulo)
values.description: (floor(x+y) mod 6 < 3) selects color A, else B. Generates ~45° stripes.

values.name: Concentric circles
values.description: if floor(d) mod 4 < 2 then ink else paper. Pure ring pattern from distance.

values.name: Color from angle
values.description: Hue varies with the angle from center: r·cos·θ, g·sin·θ, plus radial fade. atan2(y, x) gives the angle.

values.name: Circle composed over math gradient
values.previousName: Picture · circle composed over math gradient
values.description: A red circle from `circle()` overlaid on a Field that fades cyan→magenta diagonally. Mixes high-level shape with low-level math.

values.name: Y = x  (linear)
values.description: The simplest function: y = x. Diagonal line from bottom-left to top-right.

values.name: Y = x²  (parabola)
values.description: A parabola, rising symmetrically from the origin. y = x²

values.name: Y = x³  (cubic)
values.description: Cubic — rising through the origin with an inflection point. y = x³

values.name: Y = sin(x)
values.description: The canonical wave. Period 2π. y = sin(x)

values.name: Y = sin(x) + cos(2x)  (interference)
values.description: Sum of two sinusoids at different frequencies — the result has a richer shape than either alone.

values.name: Y = e^(-x²/2)  (Gaussian)
values.description: Bell curve. Peaks at x=0 with y=1, falls off symmetrically. y = exp(-x²/2)

values.name: Y = sin(x) / x  (sinc)
values.description: Sinc function. Limit at x=0 is 1; oscillates with decaying amplitude. Tiny gap at x=0 (NaN from 0/0).

values.name: Y = sin(x²)  (chirp)
values.description: Sine of x squared — frequency increases with x. Visually accelerating wave.

values.name: Y = |sin(x)|  (rectified)
values.description: Absolute value of sine — positive humps only. Common in signal processing.

values.name: Y = sqrt(x)  (square root)
values.description: Square root — defined for x ≥ 0. Slow growth, characteristic shape. Negative x produces NaN and the curve simply doesn't draw there.

values.name: Y = log(x)  (natural log)
values.description: Natural logarithm. Defined for x > 0; rises slowly, crosses 0 at x=1.

values.name: Y = floor(x)  (step function)
values.description: Floor — discontinuous step function. Not a continuous curve, but each row of the chart shows the constant value across an integer interval.

values.name: Sin(x) with gradient area below
values.previousName: Plot · sin(x) with gradient area below
values.description: Like a stock chart: area under the curve filled with a vertical gradient (cyan at top fading to dark). Above the curve is the dark background.

values.name: Parabola with stripes above
values.description: Above the parabola y=x², horizontal stripes alternate (every 4 pixels). Below is plain background. Demonstrates pattern-fill.

values.name: Cos(x) thick stroke
values.description: y = cos(x) drawn at thickness 3 (≈6-pixel-wide line). Useful when the chart is small and a thin line is hard to read.

values.name: Sin(x) dashed
values.description: y = sin(x) drawn as a dashed line — 4 pixels on, 4 pixels off, repeating along x.

values.name: Sin(x) with markers at integer multiples of π/2
values.previousName: Plot · sin(x) with markers at integer multiples of π/2
values.description: Curve plus amber circular markers at x = -2π, -3π/2, -π, -π/2, 0, π/2, π, 3π/2, 2π. Useful for highlighting key sample points.

values.name: Sin(x) with arrows along the curve
values.previousName: Plot · sin(x) with arrows along the curve
values.description: Arrow markers placed at x = -π, -π/2, 0, π/2, π, each rotated to match the local tangent direction (slope = cos(x)). Visualises 'where the curve is going' at each sample.

values.name: Parabola with arrows pointing up the slope
values.previousName: Plot · parabola with arrows pointing up the slope
values.description: y = x². Arrows at x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 each rotated to the tangent direction (slope = 2x). At x=0 the tangent is horizontal; further out the arrows tilt steeper.

values.name: Steak with overlaid circles
values.description: Sample photo (steak) with three colored circles overlaid. Demonstrates raster + vector composition: `over(circle, over(circle, over(circle, raster(image))))`.

values.name: Eye photo with heart overlay
values.previousName: Composite · eye photo with heart overlay
values.description: Eye photo with a red heart shape positioned over the iris. Heart math: (x² + y² - 1)³ - x²·y³ ≤ 0 — a real implicit curve, drawn as a Field.

values.name: Book cover with framed rectangles
values.previousName: Composite · book cover with framed rectangles
values.description: Book cover with three concentric rectangle outlines — a stylised picture frame. Each rectangle is drawn as the difference between an outer filled rectangle and an inner transparent area (achieved by clipping).

values.name: Fenel landscape with sine wave overlay
values.previousName: Composite · Fenel landscape with sine wave overlay
values.description: Sample photo with a translucent y=sin(x) curve drawn over it. The Field is transparent except on the curve, so the photo shows through everywhere else.

values.name: A4 sine (440 Hz)
values.description: Concert-A sine. The math: Wave(\t -> sin(2π·440·t)). Reference pitch.

values.name: Low bass sine (110 Hz)
values.description: A2 — two octaves below concert A. Deep low rumble.

values.name: High treble sine (1760 Hz)
values.description: A6 — two octaves above concert A. Piercing high pitch.

values.name: Sawtooth (220 Hz)
values.description: A3 sawtooth — gritty, harmonic-rich timbre. Classic synth sound.

values.name: Square (220 Hz)
values.description: A3 square wave — chiptune / 8-bit game console timbre.

values.name: C major chord
values.description: Three sines mixed: C4 (261.63), E4 (329.63), G4 (392.0). Triad — sounds harmonious.

values.name: Dissonant cluster
values.description: Three sines a semitone apart (C4, C#4, D4) — beating + clash. Jarring.

values.name: Gain · half volume
values.description: gain(0.5, sine(440)) — same A4 pitch, half amplitude. Intentional 'quieter same note' demo.

values.name: MIDI note 69 (A4)
values.description: note 69 = sine(midiToFreq 69) = sine(440). Same A4, but built via the MIDI pitch helper.

values.name: MIDI note 60 (middle C)
values.description: note 60 = sine(midiToFreq 60) ≈ sine(261.63). Middle C — centre of the keyboard.

values.name: Pitch shift up an octave
values.previousName: Sound · pitch shift up an octave
values.description: pitch(2, sine 220) — same source, played 2× faster, effectively 440 Hz. Listen to the octave jump.

values.name: Delayed echo
values.description: Mix the original sine with a delayed (and gain-reduced) copy — synthetic single-tap echo.

values.name: Bouncing ball
values.description: Red circle whose x-position oscillates: x = 16 + 12·sin(2π·t). Visible motion frame-to-frame.

values.name: Orbiting dot
values.description: Green dot orbits around centre: position = (16 + 10·cos(2π·t), 16 + 10·sin(2π·t)). Circular motion as math.

values.name: Color pulse
values.description: Solid colour cycling through the spectrum: r = 128+127·sin(t), g shifted, b shifted. Pure colour motion, no shape.

values.name: Expanding circle
values.description: Radius grows then shrinks: r = 4 + 8·|sin(π·t)|. Pulse-like breathing.

values.name: Two-circle orbit
values.description: Two circles rotating in opposite phases — composed via overAnim. Each is its own time function.

values.name: Rolling stripes
values.description: A Field whose body uses both p and t — sin((x + 8·t)·0.5). The pattern slides horizontally over time.

values.name: Bouncing ball + sine
values.description: withAudio: red ball oscillates x=16+12·sin(2π·t) while a 440 Hz sine plays. Watch the position align with the audio cycle.

values.name: Colour pulse + chord
values.description: Solid colour cycling through the spectrum as a C-major triad sustains. Pure colour + harmony.

values.name: Orbiting dot + low bass
values.description: Green dot orbits the centre while a 110 Hz bass sine drones. Visual angular motion + sustained low pitch.

values.name: C major scale
values.description: Eight notes ascending: C D E F G A B C5. Each note bounded to 0.28 s so they don't pile up.

values.name: Arpeggiated triad
values.description: C major broken chord: C E G C E G C — rolling upward 7 notes. Each plucked for 0.18 s.

values.name: Twinkle Twinkle (full first phrase)
values.description: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star · How I wonder what you are. C C G G A A G — F F E E D D C. Each note plucked.

values.name: Frère Jacques
values.description: Frère Jacques first two phrases: C D E C, C D E C, E F G, E F G. The classic round in C major.

values.name: Drone + melody
values.description: Sustained C bass underneath a five-note treble pattern. Two layers — true polyphony.

values.name: I-IV-V-I chord progression
values.description: C major → F major → G major → C major. Each chord is a 3-note triad held for 1 s. Backbone of pop/folk harmony.

values.name: Click stream
values.description: An Event with five clicks at increasing timestamps. Visualised as a list.

values.name: Accumulated count
values.description: accum(0, add, clicks) — a Behavior whose value at time t is the count of events ≤ t. Sampled at t=2 to read the running total.

values.name: Click counter
values.description: Each input event increments the state. View renders a red circle whose radius is the count. Click ▶ Play to interact.

values.name: Sonify a circle
values.description: Render a circle Picture, scan its pixels, and play them as audio. Each pixel's luminance becomes a sample.

values.name: Sonify a checkerboard
values.description: 8-pixel-tile checkerboard sonified at audio rate. Alternation between dark/light cells produces a pulse train.

values.name: Visualize a sine
values.description: Render a 440 Hz sine to a buffer, then plot its waveform as a Picture. Oscilloscope-style.

values.name: Visualize the C-major chord
values.description: Render the chord, then plot the resulting waveform — visible interference between the three sines.

values.name: Triangle stroked
values.description: Three anchors connected by line segments, stroked at thickness 2.

values.name: Triangle filled
values.description: Same triangle, filled instead of stroked. Even-odd ray-cast determines interior.

values.name: Zig-zag stroked
values.description: Five anchors connected by line segments — a zig-zag stroke.

values.name: Paddle (track input x)
values.description: State = paddle x. Each input replaces state with the input's x-coord. Click anywhere on the canvas in Play mode to move the paddle.

values.name: Score (number of clicks)
values.description: State = click count. View renders a circle whose radius is the count. Click ▶ Play and tap to grow the circle.

values.name: RunGame · interactive paddle
values.description: Wraps a Game with `runGame` — the IO bridge that surfaces the live interactive surface. The frontend recognises the LiveGame marker and renders an interactive canvas where clicks/keys feed real input events. Click anywhere to move the paddle.

values.name: Pong-ish (ball bounces in box)
values.description: State = ball x position. Each input adds delta to position; ball wraps inside [0, 32]. Use ◀ ▶ arrow keys in Play mode.
